demand.why: McKinsey and Deloitte both name change-absorption, not AI skill, as the binding constraint.
Strong survey backing but the Fed (7.3m firm-months) finds no evidence AI-adopting industries post fewer jobs. Real as a leadership anxiety, weaker as a labour fact.

demand.t: AI governance frameworks and operating models
demand.why: Annex III high-risk duties bite Dec 2027, inside the window; 1,997 US postings already 73% senior-or-above. The buyer exists today.
WEF: leadership and social influence rose 22pp in employer-stated importance between 2023 and 2025, ahead of AI and big data at 17pp.

demand.t: Building AI fluency and adoption in the workforce
demand.why: EU AI Act Art.4 in force, RBI FREE-AI asks for board and C-suite AI literacy, and PwC-FICCI puts GCC leadership literacy at 27%. Obligation plus measured gap.

demand.t: Data and AI literacy for non-technical leaders
demand.why: Real, but converging with the free tier.
Highest evidence count in the whole dataset, and the fastest to commoditise. Demand is real now and will be met cheaply by 2029.

demand.t: ESG reporting, assurance and CSRD/BRSR compliance
demand.why: India rising, Europe falling sharply. Net flat, and the two must not be averaged in a pitch.
Lightcast: a third of the average job's skills changed 2021-24, top quartile 75%. Churn roughly doubled per unit time.

demand.t: IT services, GCC and global capability centre leadership
demand.why: Global roles held from India 115 (2015) to 6,500 (2024) to a projected 30,000 by 2030. No Indian school sells this at scale.

demand.t: Cybersecurity strategy for leaders and boards
demand.why: DORA board continuing-education duty plus RBI operational-resilience training mandates.
High evidence score, but it is practitioner-certification territory (SHRM, CIPD), not business-school territory.

demand.t: Sustainability and ESG strategy for the enterprise
demand.why: Down in Europe, up in India. The CSRD omnibus cut ~42,000 companies from scope; SEBI BRSR value-chain rules push the other way.

demand.t: AI regulation and compliance (EU AI Act, DPDP, sectoral)
demand.why: Three dated regimes converge in-window: AI Act Dec 2027, DPDP 13 May 2027, RBI AI policy.

demand.t: AI in HR: hiring, development and productivity
demand.why: HR leads AI-skill posting growth at 66%, and AI in hiring and promotion is Annex III high-risk. Obligation plus adoption.

demand.t: Leading teams that include AI agents
demand.why: BCG: 65% of managers expect agents to take half their role within three years. Early market, real mechanism.
RBI mandates a board-approved AI policy with annual review; AI Act makes boards accountable.

demand.t: AI risk, safety and model assurance
demand.why: Rides the Annex III timeline with AI governance; narrower audience, so a module rather than a product.
The constraint every consultancy independently names. Rises as AI raises the change load.
Deloitte: 60% of executives use AI in decisions, 5% say they manage it well. Gap is wide and named.
DPDP substantive obligations and penalties to Rs 250 cr commence 13 May 2027.
WEF CPO Outlook now ranks job and org redesign (74%) above upskilling (70%); both land on this buyer.
Fastest-moving concept in the set. High demand, high obsolescence risk in content.
Mature, crowded, still bought.

demand.t: Evaluating AI use cases and ROI
demand.why: Follows the same cooling as AI strategy; sharper and more defensible than it.
DORA and RBI operational-resilience training mandates both bite in-window.

demand.t: Board oversight of strategy, technology and AI
demand.why: Same board accountability wave; pairs naturally with a board credential.
India indigenisation is real but the buyer is government and PSU, not open-enrolment.
PwC: 56% of CEOs see no AI financial benefit yet, which is a business-model problem, not a technology one.

demand.t: Trust, accountability and human oversight of AI decisions
demand.why: AI Act Art.14 makes human oversight a competence requirement, not a checkbox.
Independent-director obligations plus AI and ESG accountability landing on boards at once.
PLI-driven and real, but ISB's manufacturing assets sit in Munjal, outside Exec Ed.
PwC: 56% of 4,454 CEOs report no significant financial benefit from AI yet. Strategy demand holds but the narrative is cooling.

demand.t: AI and machine learning fundamentals for executives
demand.why: Same commoditisation path. Coverage play, not a margin play.
WEF CPO Outlook now ranks job and org redesign (74%) above upskilling (70%). The most under-supplied classic topic.
Holds; the growth is in the AI-in-HR topic, not the generic CHRO agenda.
CS3D Article 22 climate-transition-plan duty deleted; CEEW puts India's green jobs in deployment and O&M, with no managerial layer.
47% of midlevel managers report AI strain against 31% of executives. The load is measured, not asserted.
PwC India: contraction is at junior level, 30% say mid-level stable, 19% expect senior increases. India does not import the Western squeeze.

demand.t: Leading in the first 90 days / role transition
demand.why: IMD and IIM-C both prove the premium; steady rather than growing.

demand.t: Model observability and assurance for leaders
demand.why: 41% of AI-governance postings ask for it. No programme anywhere addresses it for a leadership audience.

demand.t: Sales leadership and sales force management
demand.why: Stable; the change is in sales ops and AI tooling, not leadership.
Perennial; ISB's asset here is an incubator brand, not a research centre.
Gains value as AI drafts more of the analysis, though the mechanism is argued rather than measured.
Perennial and the most crowded tier in the market.

demand.t: Work redesign to convert AI time savings into output
demand.why: BCG: 47% of workers now spend more time directing AI than working, and India is weakest at converting that time.
WEF keeps it top-five, but it is hard to sell as a standalone product.
Rides the same WEF social-influence delta. Rises as more routine analysis is automated.

demand.t: Digital health, health analytics and AI in medicine
demand.why: ABDM plus India's hospital-management shortage; ISB has the Max Institute.
Perennial, heavily supplied.
Perennial.

demand.t: AI for the CFO and finance function
demand.why: Finance is third in AI-skill posting growth at 40% and the CFO seat is where AI ROI gets adjudicated.

demand.t: Generative AI for marketing and creative
demand.why: High adoption, low willingness to pay at executive level; it is a practitioner product.

demand.t: Sales operations, enablement and AI in sales
demand.why: Almost no supply anywhere and a clear commercial payback story.
Carried by the same regulatory wave; the audience is the GC and CCO more than the CEO.

demand.t: Leading in uncertainty, volatility and ambiguity
demand.why: Deloitte: 85% say adaptability is critical, 7% are delivering it.
Steady institutional demand; rarely bought as an open programme.

demand.t: Geopolitics for business leaders and boards
demand.why: UNICON names it the underserved topic; IMD and MIT Sloan have both launched. Demand is real, supply is thin in India.
Cyclical rather than structural.

demand.t: General management programmes for senior leaders
demand.why: India-specific: KPMG/AIMA Management Capability Development Index fell from 76 (2011) to 69.7 (2024). Classic GM is not saturated here even as Western manager seats contract.

demand.t: Psychological safety and inclusive team culture

demand.why: Mature. AI changes the tooling, not the demand level.
India produces ~2,500 hospital-management professionals a year against 21,000 needed now and ~45,000 by 2030.

demand.t: Mini-MBA and business fundamentals for specialists

demand.why: Same caveat. Stable demand, no new driver.
